questions.q: Why does this lesson insist on naming an accountable owner as step one, before anything else?
options: Because every later step in the sequence depends on someone being clearly responsible, as the Harrow Peak case study showed
Because step one is always the easiest step to complete
Because regulations require a named owner before any inventory can legally exist
Because it has nothing to do with the rest of the program and is purely symbolic
questions.explain: The lesson frames accountability as the foundation every other step depends on, illustrated by the Harrow Peak case study needing an owner before its incident occurred.

questions.q: What does the lesson say most organizations discover during Step 2, the inventory step?
options: Shadow AI systems in active use that were never approved or assigned an owner
That they have no employees using any software at all
That their accountable owner from Step 1 is unnecessary
That risk-tiering is impossible to perform
questions.explain: The lesson specifically calls out shadow AI — unapproved, unowned systems — as a common discovery during the inventory step.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what does risk-tiering (Step 3) make possible for the rest of the program?
options: Spending governance effort where it actually matters, instead of applying the heaviest controls to every system equally
Eliminating the need for any model documentation
Skipping the inventory step entirely
Guaranteeing that no AI incident will ever occur
questions.explain: Risk tiering is described as the step that makes the rest of the program affordable by focusing effort on the systems that actually carry the most risk.

questions.q: What does the lesson say to do with the frameworks and regulations covered earlier in this course, as the final step of the program?
options: Use them as vocabulary to recognize what's relevant, then bring in legal and compliance professionals for the actual determination
Apply every framework from every jurisdiction to every system, regardless of relevance
Ignore them entirely once the technical controls are in place
Assume this course's summary is sufficient for legal compliance
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that frameworks/regulations give vocabulary and recognition, not a compliance verdict — that requires real legal expertise.

questions.q: What course does the lesson name as the next step in the Data Governance career path?
options: Data Governance Program Management
Advanced Python for Data Science
Salesforce Administration
Kafka and Event Streaming
questions.explain: The lesson's closing section names Data Governance Program Management as the next course in the path, applying this course's sequencing to the whole data estate.
